What will be the decreasing order of basic strength of the following conjugate bases ?
$\mathrm{{}^{-}OH,\ RO^{-},\ CH_3COO^{-},\ Cl^{-}}$
questions.solution:
Strong acid have weak conjugate base
Acidic strength :
$\mathrm{H{-}Cl > CH_3COOH > H_2O > R{-}OH}$
Conjugate base strength :

questions.stem:
Number of complexes from the following with even number of unpaired "d" electrons is____.
$\mathrm{[V(H_2O)_6]^{3+},\ [Cr(H_2O)_6]^{2+},\ [Fe(H_2O)_6]^{3+},\ [Ni(H_2O)_6]^{3+},\ [Cu(H_2O)_6]^{2+}}$
[Given atomic numbers : V = 23, Cr = 24, Fe = 26, Ni = 28, Cu = 29]
questions.solution:
$\mathrm{[V(H_2O)_6]^{3+} \rightarrow d^2sp^3}$
$_{23}\mathrm{V}$ :- $\mathrm{[Ar]}3d^{3}4s^{2}$
$\mathrm{V^{+3}}$ :- $\mathrm{[Ar]}3d^{2}$ , $n = 2$ (even number of unpaired $e^{-}$)
$\mathrm{[Cr(H_2O)_6]^{2+} \rightarrow sp^3d^2}$
$_{24}\mathrm{Cr}$ :- $\mathrm{[Ar]}3d^{5}4s^{1}$
$\mathrm{Cr^{+2}}$ :- $\mathrm{[Ar]}3d^{4}$ , $n = 4$ (even number of unpaired $e^{-}$)
$e_g$ : $\uparrow\ \_$ ; $t_{2g}$ : $\uparrow\ \uparrow\ \uparrow$
$\mathrm{[Fe(H_2O)_6]^{3+} \rightarrow sp^3d^2}$
$\mathrm{Fe^{3+}}$ :- $\mathrm{[Ar]}3d^{5}4s^{0}$
$n = 5$ (odd number of unpaired $e^{-}$)
$\mathrm{[Ni(H_2O)_6]^{3+} \rightarrow sp^3d^2}$
$\mathrm{Ni}$ :- $\mathrm{[Ar]}3d^{8}4s^{2}$
$\mathrm{Ni^{+3}}$ :- $\mathrm{[Ar]}3d^{7}$ , $n = 3$ (odd number of unpaired $e^{-}$)
$\mathrm{[Cu(H_2O)_6]^{2+} \rightarrow sp^3d^2}$
$\mathrm{Cu}$ :- $\mathrm{[Ar]}3d^{9}4s^{0}$
$n = 1$ (odd number of unpaired $e^{-}$)

questions.stem: The enthalpy of formation of ethane ($\mathrm{C_2H_6}$) from ethylene by addition of hydrogen where the bond-energies of C – H, C – C, C = C, H – H are 414 kJ, 347 kJ, 615 kJ and 435 kJ respectively is - __________ kJ.
questions.solution:
$\mathrm{C_2H_4(g) + H_2(g) \rightarrow C_2H_6(g)}$
$\Delta H = BE(\mathrm{C{=}C}) + 4BE(\mathrm{C{-}H}) + BE(\mathrm{H{-}H}) - BE(\mathrm{C{-}C}) - 6BE(\mathrm{C{-}H})$
$\Delta H = BE(\mathrm{C{=}C}) + BE(\mathrm{H{-}H}) - BE(\mathrm{C{-}C}) - 2BE(\mathrm{C{-}H})$
$= 615 + 435 - 347 - 2 \times 414$
$= -125\ \mathrm{kJ}$

questions.stem: The number of correct reaction(s) among the following is ________.

X g of ethylamine is subjected to reaction with $\mathrm{NaNO_2/HCl}$ followed by water; evolved dinitrogen gas which occupied 2.24 L volume at STP.
X is ______ $\times 10^{-1}$ g.
questions.solution:
$\mathrm{CH_3CH_2NH_2} \xrightarrow{\mathrm{NaNO_2 + HCl}} \xrightarrow{\mathrm{H_2O}} \mathrm{CH_3CH_2{-}OH + N_2}$ (printed under the species: Mol. wt. 45 g under ethylamine, 14 g under $\mathrm{N_2}$)
given : $\mathrm{N_2}$ evolved is 2.24 L i.e. 0.1 mole.
i.e. $\mathrm{CH_3CH_2NH_2}$ (ethyl amine) will be 4.5 g (=0.1 mole)
Hence the answer = $45 \times 10^{-1}$ g

questions.stem: The de-Broglie’s wavelength of an electron in the $4^{th}$ orbit is _______ $\pi a_0$. ($a_0$ = Bohr’s radius)
questions.solution:
$2\pi r_n = n\lambda_d$
$2\pi a_0 \frac{n^2}{Z} = n\lambda_d$
$2\pi a_0 \frac{4^2}{1} = 4\lambda_d$
$\lambda_d = 8\pi a_0$

questions.stem:
Consider the following transformation involving first order elementary reaction in each step at constant temperature as shown below.
$\mathrm{A + B} \underset{\text{Step 3}}{\overset{\text{Step 1}}{\rightleftharpoons}} \mathrm{C} \xrightarrow{\text{Step 2}} \mathrm{P}$
Some details of the above reaction are listed below.
Step | Rate constant ($\mathrm{sec^{-1}}$) | Activation energy ($\mathrm{kJ\ mol^{-1}}$)
1 | $k_1$ | 300
2 | $k_2$ | 200
3 | $k_3$ | $E_{a_3}$
If the overall rate constant of the above transformation ($k$) is given as $k = \frac{k_1k_2}{k_3}$ and the overall activation energy ($E_a$) is 400 $\mathrm{kJ\ mol^{-1}}$, then the value of $E_{a_3}$ is ______ $\mathrm{kJ\ mol^{-1}}$ (nearest integer)

2.5 g of a non-volatile, non-electrolyte is dissolved in 100 g of water at $25^\circ\mathrm{C}$. The solution showed a boiling point elevation by $2^\circ\mathrm{C}$. Assuming the solute concentration in negligible with respect to the solvent concentration, the vapour pressure of the resulting aqueous solution is _______ mm of Hg (nearest integer)
[Given : Molal boiling point elevation constant of water ($K_b$) = 0.52 K. kg $\mathrm{mol^{-1}}$, 1 atm pressure = 760 mm of Hg, molar mass of water = 18 $\mathrm{g\ mol^{-1}}$]
questions.solution:
$2 = 0.52 \times m$
$m = \frac{2}{0.52}$
According to question, solution is much diluted
so $\frac{\Delta P}{P^{o}} = \frac{n_{\mathrm{solute}}}{n_{\mathrm{solvent}}}$
$\frac{\Delta P}{P^{o}} = \frac{m}{1000} \times M_{\mathrm{solvent}}$
$\Delta P = P^{o} \times \frac{m}{1000} \times M_{\mathrm{solvent}}$
$= 760 \times \frac{\frac{2}{0.52}}{1000} \times 18 = 52.615$
$P_{s} = 760 - 52.615 = 707.385$ mm of Hg
